html:
The Mahican, or Mohicans, were an Algonquian people of the upper Hudson River valley, around today's Albany, New York. Their lands ran from Lake Champlain south to the Catskills and east to the Housatonic.

When Henry Hudson sailed up the river in 1609, they traded furs with him, and the Dutch built Fort Orange in their land in 1624 as part of New Netherland. A war with the Mohawk of the Haudenosaunee for control of that trade went badly for them, and they moved east across the river. In the 1730s many settled at the mission town of Stockbridge, Massachusetts, joined by the Wappinger and others. They later moved to New York and then to Wisconsin, where they form the Stockbridge-Munsee Community. See Mohican.
